newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arab-Israeli clashes, curses in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Arab-Israeli clashes, curses in Hebron.

text.p: Palestinian youths and Israeli soldiers exchanged stones and rubber bullets in clashes in Hebron on Saturday as Israel and the Palestinian Authority traded accusations over the West Bank unrest.

One Palestinian was wounded after soldiers fired rubber bullets and teargas at youths who pelted them with stones and bottles on the confrontation line between Israeli- and PLO-ruled parts of the city.

Hebron has been ravaged by daily clashes since a Jewish woman ignited Arab anger last week by pasting anti-Moslem placards depicting the Prophet Mohammad as a pig stamping on the Koran with one hoof and writing in it with another.
"We are Moslem youth and we defend our homeland for our Koran and religion," said Nidal Mohammad Badawi Azhur, 18, lying in a Hebron hospital with a rubber-coated metal bullet in his chest.
"I am proud to be wounded." Azhur told Reuters

The violence has overshadowed Israeli-PLO peace moves which ground to a halt in March when Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu enraged Arabs by breaking ground on a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

"Mohammad is a pig! Mohammad is a pig!" jeered some of the 400 Jewish settlers who live and study in heavily fortified enclaves in the heart of the city, tossing eggs, stones and rubbish at Arab protesters.
Several homemade petrol bombs were thrown at Israeli forces in Hebron's casbah, Israeli military sources said.
"We call on the people in Palestine to chase out the herds of settlers and make their life an unbearable hell," the militant Islamist group Hamas said in a leaflet.
Scores of Palestinians have been wounded in the clashes.

Israeli cabinet secretary Danny Naveh accused Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat of "systematically violating" a January peace deal under which Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to the PLO and demanded he put an end to the unrest.

"Arafat is playing a double game. On the one hand he instructs his men to sit with Israeli representatives...and on the other he allows his security forces to allow this violence and rioting to fester," Naveh told Israel television.
"Violence and a peace process cannot go together...we passed very severe messages to the Authority on this matter."
Palestinian West Bank Preventive Security Chief Jibril Rajoub said the PLO was not Israel's lackey.
"We don't take orders from the Israeli government and our role and mission is not to defend the racist policy of Bibi Netanyahu," Rajoub told Israel's army radio.
Top PLO negotiator Saeb Erekat said Netanyahu's settlement policies had sparked Palestinian rage.

"Every time something happens he looks for somewhere to blame...I advise Mr. Netanyahu to take one look at the mirror and he will realise where the responsibility lies," Erekat told reporters in self-ruled Ramallah.
"Netanyahu should be stopped before it is too late."
The Palestinian Authority cabinet called in a statement released on Saturday after a late-night meeting for international intervention to salvage crumbling peace moves.

"In a last attempt to salvage the peace process, (we) call for a high-level international conference to save Middle East peace from the danger of destruction and ruin into which the Israeli government, through its settlement policies and freezing of the peace process, is leading this region," it said.

Israeli leaders have condemned the anti-Moslem hate poster and police have charged a 26-year-old Jewish woman with illegally posting the signs and with endangering life by stoning an Arab car -- offences that carry a maximum 24-year sentence.
